references.text: The same prohibition against oppressing foreigners, with a reminder that the Israelites themselves were foreigners in Egypt
Reiterates the prohibition against oppressing the foreigner and refers to Israel's own experience as foreigners in Egypt
Continuation of the verse that expands the command to love the foreigner as oneself
Command to help the foreigner living among the Israelites when he becomes poor
God loves the foreigner and gives him food and clothing, therefore Israel must also love the foreigners
Prohibition against exploiting a poor and needy hired worker, whether he is an Israelite or a foreigner
Curse on anyone who perverts justice for the foreigner
The prophet Jeremiah warns against oppressing the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow
The Lord commands doing what is right toward the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow
Ezekiel accuses Jerusalem of oppressing the foreigner
In the future land, foreigners shall receive an inheritance among the tribes of Israel
The Lord will bear witness against those who oppress the foreigner
Exhortation to show hospitality to foreigners, since some have unknowingly entertained angels as guests
